course.title: Building Applications on Language Models
course.tagline: Build a tested bilingual assistant service on any language model: typed outputs, tools, grounded answers, evaluation and safety checks
course.description: Participants build a bilingual rider assistant for a fictional transit authority on top of any language model, hosted or open-weight. They call models through a provider-neutral interface, extract validated structured data from rider messages, add tool calls to a synthetic trip-status service, ground answers in a policy corpus with citations and abstention, write a small evaluation set and run the assistant against it, and add input and output checks for personal data and instruction-like text. The result is a small tested web service.
course.audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career developers who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and software engineers moving into AI work.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-102 Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects
FN-105 How Machine Learning and Language Models Work
Calls a web API from Python and handles JSON
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Compare the main model API shapes and identify what changes in code when an application switches provider or moves to a local model, given the same request written for three interfaces
outcomes.evidence: an annotated comparison table that matches the reference on message structure, tool calls and usage reporting

outcomes.text: Implement structured extraction from free-text messages with schema validation, bounded retries and a fallback path, given 300 synthetic Arabic and English rider messages and a target schema
outcomes.evidence: an extraction module with tests and a measured valid-output rate against a stated target

outcomes.text: Implement tool calling for two services with typed arguments, argument validation and handling of tool errors, given a synthetic trip-status service and a ticket-creation service
outcomes.evidence: a passing test suite that includes malformed calls, timeouts and tool errors

outcomes.text: Implement a grounded answering step that retrieves policy passages, cites them and declines when the corpus holds no answer, given 120 bilingual policy pages and 30 questions the corpus cannot answer
outcomes.evidence: answers whose citations are checked automatically and a measured abstention rate

outcomes.text: Prepare a small evaluation set and measure the assistant with code-based checks and one model-graded check validated against labels, given 40 labelled cases across extraction, tool use and grounded answers
outcomes.evidence: an evaluation run with pass rates per category and the grader's agreement with the labels

outcomes.text: Configure input and output checks for personal data, off-topic requests and instruction-like text inside retrieved content, given 30 seeded risky messages and documents
outcomes.evidence: a before-and-after table of blocked, masked and passed cases with false positives counted

outcomes.text: Build a bilingual assistant service that combines structured extraction, tool calls and grounded answers behind a tested API, given the case corpus and services, a provider-neutral client and a cost limit per 1,000 requests
outcomes.evidence: a locally runnable service whose repository README reports evaluation results and cost from two measured runs

case_study.name: Darb Transit Authority
case_study.summary: Darb Transit Authority is a fictional city transport authority with four metro lines and eight bus routes. Participants build Wasil, its bilingual rider assistant: token and cost estimates, one client for hosted and local models, versioned instructions, retries, typed extraction from 300 rider messages in Arabic, English and Arabizi, tool calls to a trip-status and a ticket service, grounded answers with citations and abstention over 120 policy pages, a 40-case evaluation set with a validated model grader, personal data masking and instruction detection, and a tested web service. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

capstone.summary: An assistant for one of three supplied cases or an approved own case, submitted as a public repository with tests, an evaluation set of at least 40 cases and a README that reports results from two measured runs, cost per 1,000 requests and known limits, followed by an eight-minute defence and four minutes of questions
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository with the service, its tests, an evaluation set of at least 40 cases with its run logs and commit history, and a README that reports results from two measured runs, cost per 1,000 requests and known limits. Then an eight-minute defence with four minutes of questions: the participant runs the evaluation, explains a failing case the assessor selects, and predicts the result of one new case the assessor adds.

examples: an OpenAI-compatible local server such as llama.cpp server or Ollama
